status_note: Verified live this session (2026-06-01): a mesh1 console killed a mesh2 node it does NOT own (no OS-process ownership) via InternalMeshFrame::Shutdown; target emitted node.stopping reason=control_op + self-tombstoned, evicted from BOTH consoles in <0.1s. The full control-op kill path. Extended into the SetState lifecycle op in sprint-21.
origin: Emerged from a user correction during sprint-17/18 work: killing a node must be a MESH CONTROL OP any console can issue to any visible node — NOT the central-orchestrator hack where admin-ui owns the OS child and TerminateProcess-es it (so it could only kill its own spawns). See memory feedback_kill_is_mesh_control_op.
objective: A console kills ANY node it can see, in ANY mesh, with NO OS-process ownership. The kill is a control op (InternalMeshFrame::Shutdown) sent to the target; the target self-terminates (node.stopping + broadcasts its own gossip tombstone + graceful exit). Supersedes the OS-ownership kill path from sprint-15.
mechanism: InternalMeshFrame::Shutdown { reason } (op_kind=control). admin-ui kill_one resolves the target's node_id+location from live_digests (own mesh) OR the backbone directory (other meshes) OR its spawn registry, then node_base::send_shutdown dials the node (direct or relay) and writes the Shutdown frame. run_bi_reader dispatches it to handle_shutdown_op → broadcast_tombstone(self) + trigger_self_shutdown → wait_for_signal returns 'control_op' → standard graceful shutdown. The killing console also broadcasts the backbone tombstone for cross-mesh eviction. No state.processes membership required.
acceptance_tests: T2 CROSS-CONSOLE / CROSS-MESH KILL (the user's scenario, MEASURED): two cross-seeded consoles — Console1 mesh1 :19100, Console2 mesh2 :19101. Console2 spawns mesh2 nodes incl a 2nd mesh2 gateway. From CONSOLE1 (mesh1, which did NOT spawn it), DELETE that mesh2 gateway. ASSERT: (a) the target OS process actually exits (pid gone); (b) it disappears from BOTH consoles' /api/topology-cache within <5s, MEASURED, with RAFKA_STALENESS_MS=120000 so the pruner cannot be the cause.

T3 CONTROL-OP SPANS (Jaeger): rafka.mesh.control.shutdown_sent on mesh1.admin-ui (op_kind=control, peer_id=target); rafka.mesh.control.shutdown_received on the target node; rafka.mesh.node.stopping (reason=control_op) on the target. Link a trace.

T4 NO OWNERSHIP REQUIRED (code): kill_one resolves the target from gossip/backbone/spawn-registry and sends a control op; grep proves it does NOT require state.processes membership and does NOT TerminateProcess-on-own-child as the kill mechanism (the only TerminateProcess is an OPTIONAL reap when the console happens to own the child).

T5 SELF-TOMBSTONE: the killed node broadcasts its OWN gossip tombstone before exit — rafka.mesh.tombstone.applied fires on its same-mesh peers (Console2) via the gossip receive path, independent of the cross-mesh backbone tombstone.
T6 UI PROOF (admin-ui IS the proof): before/after screenshots on BOTH consoles (Topology + Cache tabs) showing the mesh2 gateway present, then gone after the Console1 kill. Lead personally verifies.
supersedes: sprint-15/17 kill TRIGGER (admin-ui TerminateProcess on own Child). The tombstone EVICTION propagation (sprint-15 gossip + sprint-17 backbone) is unchanged and still used.
